rice.subject: A rice plant in ear
rice.note: Köhler's Medizinal-Pflanzen, 1887. Cropped to the tuft and its panicle; the dissection figures in the margins trace as litter.

bread.subject: A wheat plant in ear
bread.note: Köhler's Medizinal-Pflanzen, 1887. Wheat rather than a loaf: every usable illustration of bread itself is a composed plate on a printed ground, which traces as a rectangular block instead of an object.

pasta.subject: Farfalle
pasta.note: Farfalle rather than spaghetti, and a photograph rather than a plate. The period pasta charts are all composed on a printed ground, and every region of them that survives being cropped to a row is either a strip too thin to keep its proportions or a set of horizontal rods that reads as a second row of price bars. A bowtie holds its shape at any crop.

milk.subject: A dairy cow
milk.commons: File:Typical cows, Holstein, Jersey, Ayrshire, Short-horn, 1904.jpg
milk.note: Cropped to the near cow. paper=0.42 is what separates her from the meadow: the grass hatching sits above it, her markings below.

eggs.subject: A hen's egg
eggs.note: The one modern photograph in the set: no period plate of a hen's egg traces into anything legible. Padded out hard because the staple rows crop a plate to the row, and an egg that filled its frame would be cropped to a featureless middle.

sugar.subject: Sugarcane in flower
sugar.note: Flora de Filipinas, Francisco Manuel Blanco, 1880-83.

chicken.subject: A cockerel
chicken.commons: File:Gallus gallus domesticus - Zwarte Poolsche Haan 1869.jpg
chicken.note: A near-black bird on pale ground, so the two inner thresholds land inside the same ink and this plate comes out as a two-tone silhouette; trace.py handles that rather than it being forced here. Padded out for the same reason as the egg -- the middle of a silhouette is a blob.

cooking_oil.subject: A coconut palm and a split coconut
cooking_oil.note: Flora de Filipinas, Francisco Manuel Blanco, 1880-83. Coconut is the Philippine cooking oil; cropped past the habit sketch in the margin.

coffee.subject: A coffee branch in cherry
coffee.note: Flora de Filipinas, Francisco Manuel Blanco, 1880-83. Cropped past the dissection details in the margin.

bananas.subject: A banana plant with its hand of fruit
bananas.note: Flora de Filipinas, Francisco Manuel Blanco, 1880-83.

pork.subject: A Berkshire pig
pork.commons: File:Berkshire Pig • p182• Brett's Colonist's Guide 1883.tif
pork.note: Brett's Colonist's Guide, 1883. A wood-engraved Berkshire in side profile, the same register as the cow and the cockerel.

fish.subject: A milkfish
fish.note: Francis Day, Fauna of British India: Fishes, 1889. Milkfish is bangus, the Philippine staple fish; the basket line names tilapia and round scad, but the art wants the archetype.

onions.subject: Two onion bulbs
onions.note: Vilmorin-Andrieux, Les plantes potageres, 1883. The two bulbs overlap too closely to crop to one, and the pair reads truer to the basket line anyway.

cheese.subject: A block of Swiss cheese
cheese.note: Mrs Beeton's Book of Household Management, 1907 edition. Cropped to the Swiss block from a composed plate of twenty; the holes are what read as cheese at chip size.

canned_fish.subject: A sardine
canned_fish.note: Hugh McCormick Smith, 1902. The fish rather than the tin: a labelled printed object traces as a rectangle, the same failure the bread and pasta notes record.
